definition: The lowest concentration of the measurand that the analyser reliably distinguishes from zero, expressed as the limit of detection.
The coefficient of variation of repeated measurements plotted across the measuring interval of each assay cartridge.
A batch of calibrator material manufactured under one batch record and assigned one set of target values.
The single-use test unit holding the reagents for one Kestrel-3 assay run; replaces the term reagent pack.
A circumstance in which a patient, user or other person is exposed to one or more hazards from the analyser or its results.
The weighing of the clinical benefit of a Kestrel-3 result against the residual risks that remain after all risk control measures.
A user action or lack of action that leads to a different result than intended by the manufacturer or expected by the user.
A health professional trained to operate the analyser at the point of care: nurse, physician or laboratory technician.
Testing performed outside a laboratory environment by a health professional, close to the patient.
The interval over which results are proportional to the concentration of the measurand within the stated deviation.
A substance in the sample other than the measurand that changes the measured result.
The period during which an unopened cartridge, stored as labelled, keeps its stated performance.
Any identifiable part of the Kestrel-3 embedded or companion software, at any level of decomposition.
The series of numeric or alphanumeric characters on the label that identifies the analyser or cartridge model and production unit.
The ability of the analyser to yield results correlated with a particular clinical condition in the target population.
The activities that collect and review experience with the Kestrel-3 placed on the market to identify any need for action.
A person without formal training in a relevant field of health care who performs a test at home.
A result produced and read by a lay user without professional supervision.
Former name of the single-use test unit; retired 2026-11-05 in favour of Cartridge.
Former term for the reportable range; retired 2026-10-22, the analytical reports now use linearity range.
Proposed term for the matrix that maps residual risk to acceptability; not yet adopted by the glossary board.
Superseded draft entry merged into Precision profile on 2026-10-22.
Proposed synonym of near-patient testing; not adopted.
